stem: A polling firm selected 1,200 telephone numbers at random from a list of all landline numbers in a country and surveyed one adult at each number. Of those surveyed, 58% said they use online banking. Which of the following is the most likely reason this result may not be a good estimate for all adults in the country?

choices.A: A sample of 1,200 adults is too small to estimate a percent for a whole country.
choices.B: Selecting the numbers at random introduced bias into the sample.
choices.C: Adults who have no landline could not be selected, and their rate of online banking may be different.
choices.D: A result close to 50% cannot be used to describe a population.

solution: The list used to choose the sample (landline numbers) leaves out every adult without a landline.
Those adults, for example many younger adults who use only mobile phones, may bank online at a different rate, so the sample under-represents part of the population.

explanation.A: Incorrect. A random sample of 1,200 can estimate a national percent well; the problem is who could be selected.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Random selection reduces bias; the bias comes from the list the numbers were chosen from.
explanation.C: Correct. Leaving out adults without a landline (undercoverage) can bias the estimate.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Any percent from a representative sample can describe a population.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'A': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'C', 'D': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'C', 'D': 'D'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
frame = {'covers_all_adults': False, 'random_from_frame': True}
assert frame['random_from_frame'] and not frame['covers_all_adults']
ok = [k for k, v in choices.items() if 'no landline' in v]
assert ok == [answer]
